title: Automated ProofChain for Control Assertions: SOC2/ISO Evidence Lifecycle
creator: Priya Shah
description: Design and deliver an end-to-end ProofChain for compliance control assertions that automates collection, normalization, retention enforcement, and reporting of SOC 2 and ISO 27001 evidence. The feature will: map controls to platform telemetry and artifacts, provide configurable geofenced retention profiles, surface cryptographically verifiable artifacts for auditors, and integrate with existing collectors (hosting, Dedicated, Private) and the Console. Focus areas: control->artifact mapping model, collector adapters (audit logs, metrics, KV cache snapshots, rollout records), artifact normalization + classification, immutable evidence ledger (ProofChain) with tamper-evident hashes, retention enforcement engine with region-aware purging, and a reporting UI + export format for audits. Scope excludes legal policy changes and external customer-side data export tools (may be follow-ups).
acceptance_criteria: Control mapping UI and JSON schema to link SOC2/ISO controls to collector outputs established
At least three collector adapters working end-to-end (audit logs, rollout history, KV cache snapshots) producing normalized artifacts
ProofChain ledger accepts artifacts, stores tamper-evident hash, and returns cryptographic evidence for sample artifacts
Retention profile applied to artifacts results in region-aware deletion/purging in a staging environment
Console reporting page shows evidence bundles for a given control with exportable ZIP + manifest accepted by audit checklist
Automated smoke run (CI) that collects artifacts for sample control, ingests into ProofChain, and verifies manifest hashes

risks: KMS integration for signing artifacts in Private deployments may delay timeline if HSM onboarding requires legal review
Retaining compressed KV cache snapshots increases storage cost — need cost model and quota guardrails
Cross-region proof binding introduces complexity for data residency constraints (cannot copy artifacts across regions without customer consent)
Auditor acceptance risk: exported manifest must match auditor import expectations — will require early auditor touchpoints
notes: Trade-off considered: full immutable append-only ledger vs tamper-evident hash store. Chosen: minimal ledger storing hash + metadata with optional external append-only store for enterprise customers to reduce storage and simplify purging.

We will reuse existing collector framework where possible; new adapter interface will be backwards compatible. Collectors should emit 'artifact' JSON with required fields: artifact_id, control_ids, timestamp, region, signer_hash
Plan to stage feature behind 'proofchain' license flag for Dedicated/Private customers initially
Follow-ups: add automated auditor access portal (PM-23010) and evidence aging dashboard (ENG-5201)
